card.name: Abstract value or merit nouns
card.fires_on: Abstract words about worth, merit or satisfaction, such as value, authority, thrill, rewarding, explains and glory, in essays and religious or philosophical prose. Usually just before 'of' or a following clause.

modes.label: Worth and value nouns
modes.description: Nouns naming the value or worth of something, often followed by 'of'.
modes.example: What is the<< value>> of Flying Foxes?

modes.label: Moral or religious terms
modes.description: Religious or moral words, including the middle of 'sanctified'.
modes.example: the unbelieving wife is sanct<<ified>> through her believing husband

modes.label: Reward and satisfaction words
modes.description: Words about reward, thrill or authority of an experience or idea.
modes.example: still he says the<< thrill>> of sharing a dive with his son outweigh

card.plain: It lights up on abstract words about the worth, reward or authority of something in essay-style writing.
